Role of Artificial Intelligence in Radiation Oncology: A Missed Opportunity for LMICs?
source: PubMed · International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
desc: [International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics] Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are driving a major shift in modern medicine, particularly within radiation oncology. AI in radiation oncology offers low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) a way to offset critical shortages of oncologists and physicists by automating segmentation, planning, and quality checks, improving efficiency, and expanding equitable access to care. Its actual value depends on validation against LMICs' infrastructure and patient populations, an area where current evidence remains limited. This review aims to comprehensively summarize the current evidence on AI and ML applications across key domains of radiotherapy, while highlighting global disparities in adoption, particularly in LMICs. This critical review conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for studies published between 2010 and April 2026. Only relevant studies emphasizing the efficiency of AI in radiation workflow and the existing gaps in its adoption within LMICs were included in this review. Eleven studies published between 2019 and 2025 were included. Study designs comprised original research (n=5), reviews (n=4), a survey (n=1), and a study protocol (n=1). Studies were conducted across multiple LMICs in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, predominantly evaluating AI-based contouring and treatment-planning tools, with Radiation Planning Assistant (RPA) being the most frequently reported platform. AI tools demonstrated comparable performance in LMICs relative to High-Income Countries (HICs), particularly with regard to time efficiency and the quality of target volume contouring. Yet the majority of LMICs still don't have AI tools in their radiation centers to work efficiently. The current literature reveals a gap between the need for AI in radiation oncology in LMICs and the available evidence supporting its implementation. LMICs could benefit substantially from AI-enabled improvements in radiation oncology. Several conclusions about the applicability of these findings in LMIC settings were drawn by extrapolation from studies conducted in HIC contexts, which substantially limits their direct generalizability to lower-resource environments. Cost-effective and accessible AI models hold promise to address workforce shortages, improve efficiency, and expand equitable access to quality radiotherapy services.

title: Learning Scientific Trajectories to Predict Future Biomedical Discoveries
desc: AI co-scientists have expanded the use of large language models for generating scientific hypotheses and guiding experimental investigation. Here we investigate whether temporal patterns in the semantic representations of complete biomedical conclusions can guide hypothesis generation. We introduce ForeSCITE, a framework that identifies thematic clusters of published conclusions, estimates a direction separating earlier from more recent findings within each cluster, and projects existing conclusion embeddings along these directions. An embedding language model trained to reconstruct conclusions decodes the projected coordinates into natural-language hypotheses. Across 407 clusters derived from approximately three million pre-cutoff conclusions, we identify temporal structure and illustrate its retention after decoding. In retrospective, time-sliced evaluations, ForeSCITE increases semantic coverage beyond the historical corpus, biomedical entity-pair novelty and post-cutoff pair re-observation relative to five prompt-based and retrieval-augmented baselines. Expert review of prioritized CAR-T hypotheses identified 37 candidates as both novel and biologically plausible, and expert justifications for five selected hypotheses illustrate their biological rationale and subsequent literature support where available. These findings support temporal guidance in semantic space as a scalable mechanism for proposing biomedical hypotheses for subsequent scientific evaluation.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Cleft and Craniofacial Care.
source: PubMed · Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America
desc: [Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into cleft and craniofacial care to facilitate objective assessment, optimize treatment planning, and improve outcome evaluation. By leveraging 3-dimensional imaging, machine learning, and automated workflows, AI addresses key clinical challenges such as anatomic variability, limited robust normative references, and reliance on subjective expertise. Recent developments enable streamlined data acquisition and automated design of surgical devices. This article reviews current applications and highlights clinically relevant advances toward integrated digital workflows and emerging digital twin concepts, with the goal of improving precision, efficiency, and accessibility across cleft and craniofacial treatment pathways.

title: Latent Decision Flow Rewards for Clinical Guideline Reasoning
desc: Clinical practice guidelines encode evidence-based recommendations as conditional decision flows, which makes them a natural source of process supervision for training reasoning models. Two properties of clinical reasoning make this supervision difficult to use. A decision flow consistent with a guideline does not by itself determine the correct answer for a given patient, which we call the path--answer gap, and several valid decision flows can support the same clinical decision, which we call path multiplicity. Current training approaches address parts of this problem. Answer rewards supervise the final decision, and process rewards computed against a reference flow supervise one valid decision flow per case. Supervised fine-tuning on annotated flows teaches guideline-consistent reasoning but constrains the model to one trajectory per case and can reduce answer accuracy. We introduce GUIDER, a method that jointly optimizes a decision flow controller and a reasoning policy. The controller learns to generate plausible decision flows from guideline-derived supervision, and the policy learns to generate a decision flow and a final answer for each patient case. GUIDER computes the process reward for the policy over several controller-generated flows, which accounts for path multiplicity, and gates this reward on answer correctness, which addresses the path--answer gap. Joint training allows the process supervision to evolve with the policy. On MedGUIDE, GUIDER with Qwen3-14B achieves 82.5 weighted accuracy and 73.5 guideline adherence, 3.3 and 3.1 points above the strongest clinical reinforcement learning baseline. With Qwen3-14B and Gemma4-12B backbones, GUIDER also improves over CRPO, MRPO, and FaithMed on the out-of-domain benchmarks AMEGA-LLM, RealMedQA, and CancerGUIDE.

title: Beyond a single ratio: an adaptable deep learning approach to analyze the prognostic value of TSP distribution in ovarian cancer.
desc: [The Journal of pathology] The tumor-stroma percentage (TSP) has been proposed as a prognostic factor in ovarian cancer. When assessed manually by pathologists, the TSP can be subject to significant inter-rater variability. Automated methods for TSP determination have recently been developed. Existing approaches typically yield a single TSP value for a relatively small region of interest in the slide, introducing bias through region selection and potentially overlooking the TSP distribution across the entire histologically examined area. We present an adaptable deep learning pipeline, efficiently fine-tuned for ovarian cancer tissue analysis using a few-shot learning approach, requiring only minimal new training annotations. Instead of calculating a single TSP value, our method quantifies the global TSP distribution across the entire tumor and therefore captures its spatial heterogeneity. To identify a prognostic biomarker, we systematically evaluated a panel of metrics describing this distribution in 98 patients. Our analysis revealed that the mean-median difference of the TSP distribution [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.60, 95% CI = 0.46-0.79, p < 0.001], a quantitative measure of asymmetry, together with the mean TSP (HR = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.43-0.97, p = 0.03), are biomarkers significantly associated with recurrence-free survival. By successfully adapting a pipeline for ovarian cancer, we demonstrate that automated analysis of the entire TSP distribution provides significant prognostic information superior to that obtained by manual assessment. Spatial heterogeneity of the TSP is a key prognostic factor. © 2026 Fraunhofer IIS and The Author(s). title: Visually Irrelevant Hallucinations in Medical Vision-Language Models
desc: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show strong performance in radiology report generation (RRG) and medical visual question answering (Med-VQA), producing free-form clinical descriptions and answers from medical images. However, they may generate clinically meaningful statements that lack visual evidence or contradict image content. We refer to these errors as visually irrelevant hallucinations and investigate them at the phrase level. We propose CLEAR (Counterfactual Localized Evaluation of Alignment and Response), a model-agnostic post-hoc framework for phrase-level hallucination risk estimation. CLEAR decomposes generated responses into visually assessable clinical phrases. For each phrase, phrase-conditioned grounding identifies a candidate visual region, which is selectively perturbed by a localized counterfactual intervention. CLEAR characterizes the intervention using two complementary auditing cues: response cues, capturing semantic and clinically meaningful changes in the generated response, and alignment cues, measuring changes in image-phrase compatibility. These cues are normalized and jointly modeled to estimate phrase-level hallucination risk. Across four datasets spanning RRG and Med-VQA, CLEAR outperforms state-of-the-art hallucination detection baselines across multiple medical and general-purpose VLMs. On MIMIC-CXR, CLEAR improves AUPRC from 85.10% to 90.23%. Its effectiveness is further validated on a GT-derived controlled VIH benchmark. These results establish visually irrelevant hallucination as an important fine-grained reliability failure mode in medical VLMs and demonstrate the value of model-agnostic visual-support auditing for more trustworthy multimodal clinical generation.

title: 7 T MRI in moyamoya disease: current evidence and AI-assisted future directions-a narrative review.
desc: [Frontiers in neurology] Infographic summarizes the use of 7T MRI in Moyamoya disease, showing individualized assessment, current standard-of-care, high-resolution microvascular phenotyping, evidence gaps, candidate clinical outputs, and AI-assisted future directions like feature extraction, segmentation, multimodal integration, and risk modeling, with relevant icons and MRI images.

title: CARF: Context-Aware Reasoning Supervision for Scientific Evidence Screening
desc: Systematic reviews synthesize biomedical evidence to inform clinical and public-health decision-making, but require domain experts to manually screen thousands of studies against detailed eligibility criteria. We investigate whether language models can assist with this bottleneck by learning from expert feedback on title and abstract screening decisions and model-generated reasoning. We introduce the Context-Aware Reasoning Framework (CARF), a human-in-the-loop framework that uses expert feedback on model-generated reasoning to adapt language models to context-dependent screening tasks. We evaluate CARF on systematic reviews of verbal autopsy and cause-of-death ascertainment methods used in global public health mortality surveillance. CARF shows competitive screening performance compared to evaluated models while retaining high sensitivity, and is more inclined to retain ambiguous, context-dependent studies for human review. Together, these findings suggest that expert-corrected reasoning is a promising supervision signal for context-dependent scientific screening, while retaining a role for human oversight.

title: Artificial intelligence policies in academic primary health care: a review of journals and their publishers.
source: PubMed · Primary health care research & development
desc: [Primary health care research & development] The rapid adoption of AI tools in academic research has created uncertainty about appropriate use in manuscript preparation, particularly in primary health care where clear guidance is essential for maintaining research integrity across diverse settings. This review aimed to assess the availability and content of AI policies across primary health care journals and their publishers. We identified primary health care journals through searches of SCImago Journal & Country Rank, Google Scholar, and a Google search. After screening for English language, functioning webpages, recent publications, and exclusion of predatory journals, 41 journals were included. Two reviewers independently reviewed journal homepages, author guidelines, submission policies, and editorial policies for AI-related statements at both journal and publisher levels between 18 and 21 July 2025. Of 41 journals assessed, 33 (80.5%) had publicly available AI policies - 21 (51.2%) at journal level and 12 (29.3%) at publisher level. Eight journals (19.5%) had no identifiable public AI policy. All identified policies were permissive toward AI use but varied in requirements across five key areas: disclosure of AI use, acceptable AI tasks, AI authorship considerations, author responsibility, and peer review guidelines. While most primary health care journals have established AI policies, significant gaps remain in accessibility and standardization. The fragmented governance landscape, characterized by inconsistent policy locations and requirements, creates confusion for authors and might compromise research integrity. Standardized, easily accessible AI policies are needed to enable researchers to harness AI's potential while maintaining transparency and scientific rigour essential to primary health care research.

title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups
desc: Quantum machine learning (QML) is increasingly explored for medical classification, yet its behaviour under subgroup-aware fairness criteria remains understudied. We present an empirical fairness audit of classical and quantum classifiers for medical imaging, assuming QML is not inherently fair. Two scenarios are evaluated: dermatological lesions on DDI (sensitive attribute: Fitzpatrick skin type) and chest X-rays on CheXpert-derived data (sensitive attribute: age group). Using ResNet-18 embeddings, we train SVM, MLP, QSVM and QCNN under a baseline and three mitigation settings: differentiable Equalized Odds (EO) regularisation, Gradient Reversal Learning (GRL), and both combined. Foundation models (PanDerm, EVA-X) serve as external references. Quantum classifiers may achieve competitive aggregate performance while still exhibiting subgroup disparities. Since a smaller subgroup AUC gap may stem from degrading the best group rather than improving the worst, each mitigation is also tested against a pre-specified non-inferiority margin relative to its baseline. Under this criterion, several configurations with the smallest disparity, notably QCNN with GRL on DDI, are not clinically acceptable due to loss of global discrimination. On DDI, QSVM with GRL+EO performed best and approached PanDerm in the performance/fairness trade-off; on CheXpert, QCNN with GRL achieved the highest aggregate performance but increased disparity, and EVA-X remained stronger. Fairness effects are model- and dataset-dependent, so QML requires empirical subgroup-aware evaluation. All quantum models run in classical simulation; we claim no quantum advantage.

title: Data-efficient deep learning surrogate modeling for finite element prediction in dental implant biomechanics.
source: PubMed · Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
desc: [Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering] Finite element analysis (FEA) is widely used to evaluate dental implant biomechanics but is computationally demanding. This study explores deep learning surrogate models for accurate stress prediction with limited data. A neural network was pre-trained on standard implant simulations (N = 3000) and adapted to narrow-diameter implants in atrophic bone (N = 200). Negative transfer occurred with extremely limited data (N = 20) due to biomechanical domain shift. However, both transfer learning and standard training achieved high accuracy at N ≥ 60 (R² = 0.94). This framework enables rapid, data-efficient biomechanical prediction for dental implant modeling.

title: Benchmarking decision models against generative large language models on medical multiple-choice questions
desc: Medical workflows often require selecting among predefined options. We compared 13 decision models with 15 generative large language model configurations, including different reasoning settings, using 1,273 four-option MedQA questions under text-only conditions. Accuracy ranged from 67.71% to 89.08% for decision models and from 78.32% to 96.86% for generative configurations. Among the tested configurations, Mercury Decide had the lowest mean final-attempt cost (USD 0.0069 per 1,000 questions), while Clef Omni had the shortest median request duration (0.291 seconds). Decision-model probabilities distinguished correct from incorrect answers, but error rates among answers assigned probabilities of at least 0.90 ranged from 1.71% to 12.77%. Answer agreement across three runs ranged from 92.30% to 100%, while probability repeatability varied. Decision models offered resource advantages alongside lower peak accuracy; selecting models for medical workflows requires considering probability quality and repeatability together with accuracy and the resources needed to detect and correct errors.

title: From off-target to on-demand: Precision engineering and translational evaluation of next-generation base editors.
desc: [Biotechnology advances] Due to the increasing demand for clinical gene therapy and the limitations of current treatment methods, there is an urgent need to develop gene-editing tools that are safer, more precise, and more clinically implementable. Deaminase-based base editors have emerged as gene-editing platforms with significant therapeutic potential because they can achieve precise single-base substitutions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks. However, the challenges of applying base editing in clinical practice extend beyond whether the intended edit can be achieved. The critical question is whether the editing system can reliably provide predictable, controllable, and verifiable outcomes across complex sequence contexts, diverse cell environments, and actual delivery conditions. This review focuses on the engineering optimization and clinical translation of base editors. We first systematically analyze the major factors affecting the clinical translation of base editors across four dimensions: editing efficiency, editing precision, safety, and delivery, together with the corresponding optimization strategies. We then summarize the applications of artificial intelligence and computational approaches in base editor design, screening, and risk assessment. We further discuss the ex vivo and in vivo pathways for clinical translation, including their respective requirements for product quality and safety evaluation. Finally, based on representative clinical programs, we discuss how editing performance, safety, and delivery factors influence development decisions for candidate base-editing systems across different therapeutic contexts, and propose minimum reporting recommendations to improve the consistency of key data and cross-study comparability.

title: DES-JEPA: Learning a Shared Vocabulary for High-Dimensional Discrete Event Sequences
desc: Temporal foundation models such as Chronos and TimesFM generalize across domains through a shared numerical observation space. In contrast, discrete event sequences (DESs), including operational event logs or patient clinical-event trajectories, have domain-specific event vocabularies whose labels lack a consistent correspondence across domains. Beyond this lack of consistency, the number of distinct events in real-world settings is high enough to challenge both classical temporal point process modeling and current in-context foundation inference models such as FIM-PP. Critically, current foundation models for DESs are limited to a small, fixed number of event types, restricting their applicability to realistic, high-dimensional event streams. To address this, we propose two complementary modules: (i) DES-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture that learns a shared discrete vocabulary from synthetic stochastic processes with unaligned event vocabularies; and (ii) DES-PFN, a discrete event sequence prior-fitted network that reuses the learned vocabulary for in-context next-event prediction. Without task-specific fine-tuning, this framework achieves competitive zero-shot performance on eight unseen real-world datasets and scales up to 700 distinct event types.

title: Data science in ecosystem-service research: A CICES-based bibliometric mapping and decision-support synthesis.
desc: [Journal of environmental management] Data science (DS) methods have attracted growing attention in ecosystem-services (ES) research, yet their bibliographic visibility across service categories and the implications of this pattern for environmental management remain insufficiently understood. This study combines bibliometric analysis, CICES-based classification, association-rule analysis, and decision-oriented synthesis to examine how DS methods are represented across ES domains. Bibliographic records were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection for 2015-2025. After LLM-assisted relevance screening, CICES-based classification, and manual validation, 53,227 ES publications were retained. We analyze temporal publication trends, geographical and institutional patterns, collaboration networks, service-domain distributions, and the bibliographic visibility of DS terms in titles, abstracts, author keywords, and Keywords Plus. Association-rule analysis was used to identify recurring ES theme-DS method associations using appearance, lift, and confidence. The results show sustained growth in ES publications and geographically uneven research output. DS-related terms were identified in 9.56% of publications under the broad bibliographic-field indicator and in 3.17% under the keyword-field indicator. Their visibility increased over time but remained concentrated in established methods. Random forest and principal component analysis were prominent among the highest-scoring theme-method associations, whereas deep learning, generative models, and explainable artificial intelligence appeared less prominently. The results suggest that established DS can support prediction, classification, and dimensionality reduction, but effective decision support requires validation, uncertainty characterization, interpretability, representativeness assessment, and accountability safeguards. The findings highlight the need to align ES questions, analytical tasks, data structures, validation strategies, management scales, and intended uses when designing DS applications for environmental management.

title: LLMs as Judges and Examinees for Medical Item Difficulty Prediction
desc: Predicting medical item difficulty from item text alone remains challenging. Prior work has largely relied on linguistic features or text representations derived from general-purpose and domain-specific language models, but predictive performance has remained modest. This study takes a different approach by using difficulty-related signals that emerge when open-weight large language models (LLMs) interact with test items. Using USMLE and PANCE medical licensure examination items, we examined LLMs in two roles. As judges, the models provided absolute difficulty ratings and pairwise difficulty comparisons. As simulated examinees, they generated response-based signals including correctness, keyed-option probability, response entropy, and the probability margin between the top two options. We then combined the strongest judgment and response signals with baseline item features in downstream prediction models. Pairwise difficulty judgment was the most consistent individual LLM signal across both datasets, while simulated-examinee signals and absolute judgments provided complementary information in some feature combinations. The best configurations reached a Spearman correlation of $ρ$ = .447 on USMLE, exceeding the best system in the 2024 BEA shared task ($ρ$ = .25), and $ρ$ = .494 on PANCE. These results were comparable to direct absolute judgments from the proprietary frontier model Claude Opus 5 ($ρ$ = .443 and .488, respectively). Overall, judgment and response signals from open-weight LLMs captured difficulty-related information beyond text representations. Because these models can be deployed locally, the approach offers a practical option for predicting the difficulty of unreleased or high-security test items.

title: AAV-CapNet: Multi-Omics Deep Learning with Fourier Enhancement and Cross-Attention for Predicting Infectivity of Known AAV Capsid Variants.
desc: [Viruses] This work builds AAV-CapNet, a deep learning model integrating Fourier frequency enhancement and cross-attention fusion, to predict the infectivity of 20 AAV capsid variants across 52 cancer cell lines with a self-built multi-omics dataset of 392 validated measurements. Validated via stratified splitting and repeated five-fold cross-validation, it extracts dual-domain capsid features fused with host transcriptomics for joint classification and regression. The model exhibits favourable performance under low-false-positive-rate conditions suitable for high-throughput screening. Attention mapping and ablation tests validate core modules' necessity. Despite poor generalization to unseen serotypes, this interpretable tool facilitates intraserotype capsid screening and rational engineering.

title: PulmoWorld: An Asynchronous Multimodal Medical World Model for Longitudinal Pneumonia Dynamics
desc: Pneumonia changes across respiration, inflammation, and organ function, while the measurements that describe it arrive at different times and are often incomplete. We introduce PULMOWORLD, a world model for longitudinal pneumonia dynamics that connects asynchronous state estimation, recursive simulation, and evidence-constrained planning. History-aware filtering separates state propagation from observation-driven correction, so a measurement updates the shared belief only when it is observed. That belief supports recursive forecasts of clinical values and modality representations, and summaries of future prognosis. Cap-MBRL searches imagined continuations inside an authorized action set and replaces a frozen fallback only when a candidate meets the risk budget and a predicted-cost margin. On the pneumonia cohort MASS, recursive forecasts are competitive with task-trained sequence models, and simulated future states retain prognostic information. Trained separately on public MIMIC-IV-CXR chest radiographs and clinical trajectories, this model improves prognostic discrimination over latest-value fusion in development and is competitive on long-horizon error on the locked pneumonia panel. In five known-mechanism MASS-Syn environments, Cap-MBRL lowers selection regret relative to direct fallback execution.

title: AI-guided discovery and expansion of the human bile acid landscape.
desc: [Cell metabolism] Bile acids represent one of nature's most chemically diverse and therapeutically important metabolite families. However, the human bile acid metabolome remains largely uncharted, with analytical limitations obscuring potentially thousands of biologically active species present in cells and biofluids. Here, we present MetLLM, a transformer-based language model that learns bile acid modification patterns to prioritize candidate bile acid analogs, and MetSpace, an in silico bile acid chemical landscape containing 3,900 prioritized candidates. Liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry analysis of human feces confirmed multiple newly detected and structurally novel bile acids, including MS2141 and MS1281. In vitro functional validation showed that MS2141 modulates M2 receptor-associated Gi/o signaling and alters electrophysiological parameters in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. This work expands the searchable bile acid metabolome and provides a computational framework for systematic metabolite discovery.

title: Rubricon: Automated Rubric Generation and Refinement for LLM Evaluation and Training
desc: Rubrics enable reward assignment on tasks without verifiable answers, but are expensive to manually produce from scratch. We present Rubricon, a pipeline that generates discriminative rubrics without requiring human preference labels, rubric annotation, or generator-model training. Using any LLM, Rubricon samples multiple rubrics, selects the most discriminative candidate, adds criteria to capture overlooked requirements or response flaws, and prunes criteria that are misaligned or shallow. Alongside LLM self-critique and test-time scaling, Rubricon uses observed criterion pass rates on example model responses to guide refinement. Across five professional, consumer, clinical, and general-use LLM benchmarks, Rubricon produces rubrics whose scores of frontier LLM responses exhibit 9% greater alignment with labor-intensive expert-authored rubrics, compared to the best alternative synthetic rubric generation method among RRD, QSRG, OpenRubrics, and agentic generation via harnesses like Codex. On HealthBench, post-training a Qwen3.5-9B model with Rubricon rubrics yields 4.5% better performance than training with rubrics from the strongest alternative synthetic rubric generator, RRD.

title: An Adversarial Deep Learning Framework for Non-Rigid Brain MRI Registration in Brain Shift Compensation.
source: PubMed · Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
desc: [Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie] Accurate compensation for intra-operative brain shift remains a fundamental challenge in neurosurgical procedures, as misalignment between pre-operative and intra-operative images can lead to suboptimal surgical guidance. In this work, we propose a bidirectional, unsupervised 3D brain shift compensation framework for non-rigid MRI registration, designed to directly estimate dense deformation fields between pre-operative and intra-operative volumes. The proposed approach employs dual image-translation pathways coupled with a dedicated deformation field predictor, enabling robust alignment without requiring paired training data. A key component of the framework is the integration of bidirectional consistency constraints to enforce anatomical correspondence across domains, while deformation field estimation is explicitly optimized for registration accuracy. In addition, we incorporate a Haar wavelet-based perceptual similarity (HaarPSI) loss to improve the preservation of fine-scale anatomical structures during registration. The proposed method is evaluated against classical and state-of-the-art baselines, including Elastix, Voxelmorph, and several adversarial and GAN-based learning approaches adapted with comparable registration modules. Qualitative analyses of deformation fields and error maps further demonstrate improved alignment in regions most affected by brain shift. These results highlight the effectiveness of bidirectional deformation modeling combined with adversarial and perceptual constraints for accurate, physically plausible, and unsupervised 3D non-rigid registration in neurosurgical applications.

title: Convex Potential Learning for Optimal Transport Between Medical Images
desc: Computing optimal transport maps between medical images plays a fundamental role in morphological analysis. However, existing methods are either difficult to scale to large 3D medical images or rely on regularized formulations that provide only approximate transport maps. To improve the accuracy of downstream medical image analysis, we propose a novel approach for estimating optimal transport maps by parameterizing the convex potential function. By construction, the resulting transport map is guaranteed to be curl-free, consistent with Brenier's theorem. We evaluate the proposed method on both 2D and 3D medical imaging datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves lower transport estimation errors and produces higher-quality image reconstructions than existing methods.

title: Applying Deep Learning to Image and IMU Sensor Data for Real-Time Fatigue Recognition in Table Tennis Players.
desc: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] Fatigue during table tennis training can impair performance and increase the risk of injury. This study proposes a real-time fatigue recognition system that integrates an embedded edge-AI racket with a camera for synchronized multimodal data acquisition. On the racket side, a neural network was deployed on an edge-AI microcontroller unit (MCU) to enable on-device inference, while the test data were transmitted to a computer for multimodal feature fusion. Given the continuous nature of fatigue development, the data were divided into three stages: non-fatigue, transition, and fatigue to facilitate progressive evaluation. In the binary classification task, which distinguished between the two extreme states, the multimodal hybrid model achieved an accuracy of 99%. When the transition stage was incorporated into a three-class classification task, performance declined because of the ambiguous boundaries between fatigue states. However, the use of multimodal decision-fusion strategies, such as weighted soft voting, maintained an accuracy of 96%. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of deep learning for real-time fatigue recognition during table tennis training and provide a practical monitoring tool to help players track their physiological states and reduce injury risk.

title: EUReCA: End-to-End Unified CBCT Reconstruction Across Clinical Acquisitions
desc: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is widely used for image-guided radiotherapy, but reducing the number of projections to lower dose and scan time makes reconstruction increasingly ill-posed. We present EUReCA (End-to-end Unified REconstruction across Clinical Acquisitions), a geometry-aware feed-forward model for variable-view clinical linac CBCT. For a given acquisition trajectory, EUReCA accepts 8-100 projections with a single set of weights, without view-count-specific retraining; the same architecture and training recipe extend unchanged to other clinical trajectories. It combines learned projection features with an in-frame Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstruction. The model encodes each projection with a shared multiscale backbone, back-projects features into multiresolution 3D grids using the acquisition geometry, aggregates variable numbers of views at fixed computational cost, and refines the volume with a global 3D transformer and multilevel decoder. On simulated data, EUReCA achieved 29.9-33.2 dB PSNR with 10-100 views and outperformed all applicable feed-forward baselines; it also exceeded iterative optimization-based methods while running orders of magnitude faster. On 15 measured patient CBCT scans evaluated against vendor reconstructions, EUReCA achieved the best performance at every tested view count. These results suggest that geometry-aware, measurement-anchored feed-forward reconstruction can provide a practical and flexible foundation for variable-view linac CBCT.

title: Artificial intelligence in upper-limb, language and cognitive neurorehabilitation after stroke.
desc: [Current opinion in neurology] Artificial intelligence (AI) is being increasingly integrated into upper-limb, language and cognitive neurorehabilitation research and there is interest in where the research currently lies along the pipeline towards clinical implementation and real-world impact. Across these three domains of neurorehabilitation, the research into the use of AI has shown clear potential to enhance assessment, personalize rehabilitation and extend access to care but is yet to demonstrate clinical utility and superiority over other digital rehabilitation approaches. There remain concerns about small and selective datasets being used for modelling, privacy and equity issues and sustainable implementation. It is suggested that AI should be positioned as an important tool in the clinical infrastructure rather than an autonomous clinical decision maker within clinical practice. Future research across these neurorehabilitation domains should consider implementation risks and needs early in the research pipeline, by using ethical principles and guidelines to ensure transparency and consumer involvement in AI research and implementation into clinical practice.

title: Auditable Hierarchical Inference with Multimodal Evidence and Bayesian Active Inquiry
desc: Most multimodal classifiers assume that all useful evidence is available upfront, whereas clinical inquiry is sequential. We present a synthetic evaluation framework separating objective multimodal inference from active inquiry. An objective model maps synthetic tongue, bilateral multipressure pulse, and acoustic observations to eight syndrome families. A provenance-bearing Knowledge Core and training-only answer model support Bayesian narrowing over 33 fine terms using 25 typed questions, while seven safety questions remain outside the diagnostic posterior. Weak shared symptom factors limit fine-term influence on objective phenotypes, and an objective-only probe tests leakage. In a preregistered 600-case synthetic evaluation, objective family accuracy was 87.0%. Cost-sensitive expected information gain (cost-EIG) raised family accuracy to 95.5% and exact fine-term accuracy to 42.5%, versus 92.7% and 33.0% for an unoptimized fixed-order baseline. Selective family accuracy reached 96.9% at 95.3% coverage. However, cost-EIG asked more questions on average than fixed order (9.795 versus 9.352). Missing-audio routing retained 94.0% family accuracy, and a workflow invariant enforced abstention when all objective modalities were absent. Permuting fine-term answer likelihoods reduced family accuracy to 78.7%. Five of six frozen checks passed, but the question-efficiency hypothesis failed. Comparisons are descriptive because only aggregate, not paired case-level, outputs were retained. These results establish a reproducible synthetic workflow, not clinical diagnostic or treatment validity.

title: The "Best of 2026 List" of Health Promotion Researchers.
source: PubMed · American journal of health promotion : AJHP
desc: [American journal of health promotion : AJHP] Each year the editorial team of the American Journal of Health Promotion selects our "Best of the Year List" of health promotion studies from the prior year. This editorial features the Editor's Picks Awards, the Editor in Chief Awards, the Michael P. O'Donnell Award and the Dorothy Nyswander Award for the best research and writing published in 2026 in this journal. Our criteria for selection includes: whether the study addresses a topic of timely importance in health promotion, the research question is clearly stated and the study methods used are well executed; whether the paper is often cited and downloaded; if the study findings offer a unique contribution to the literature; and if the paper is well-written and enjoyable to read. Awardees in 2026 brought our journal's readers timely perspectives on the role of artificial intelligence in addressing mental health, the role of public policy in supporting caregivers, the pernicious effects of misinformation on our views of research findings and the wonderful contributions story-telling can make in effective health education. This "best of 2026 list" featured studies based in low-income neighborhoods, healthcare delivery systems, workplaces and mental health agencies and includes case studies and qualitative and quantitative research methods that enabled researchers to better explain what helps or hinders well-being.

title: Alpha-TCM: A Nine-Layer Framework for TCM-Guided Multimodal Inference and Structured-Prior Auditing
desc: Alpha-TCM makes two contributions under a central thesis: auditable systems should separate domain knowledge, case evidence, probabilistic inference, and downstream authority. First, it proposes a nine-layer TCM-oriented architecture covering semantic definitions, multimodal acquisition, quality control, provenance-bearing knowledge, probabilistic inference, longitudinal updating, constrained decisions, language interaction, and human governance. Each layer specifies its information contract, failure boundary, dependencies, and validation status. This is a system-design proposal, not a claim of complete clinical implementation. Second, a controlled synthetic prototype instantiates Layers 1-5 to audit the knowledge-evidence interface. Four conditional-Gaussian encoders process synthetic tongue images, pulse waveforms, inquiry fields, and text, while a frozen bridge predicts a five-dimensional synthetic outcome. A versioned contextual prior is compiled independently of the renderer. Fusion removes duplicated reference-prior information before adding context. Equal-information controls, prior regularization, graded contamination, and structural corruption test contextual benefits, Bayesian specificity, and conflict detection. Across ten paired seeds and four training sizes, contextual knowledge improved mean absolute error over marginal committee fusion at 600 and 1,200 cases, but not over equal-information neural controls. Fully incorrect context harmed performance at every size, while prior effects were inconsistent and conflict scores did not track case-level damage. The results support contextual structure in low-data synthetic settings, not a specifically Bayesian advantage. The prototype establishes no claims about TCM theory or clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic, causal, longitudinal, or transfer validity.

title: The Reverse Native-Speaker Problem: Teaching Physiology to a Generation Fluent in Tools We Are Still Learning.
desc: [Advances in physiology education] Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping physiology education, but the central challenge is epistemic, not technological. Learners are often more fluent with AI tools than their instructors, yet less fluent in the physiology those tools describe: a pattern this Perspective terms the reverse native-speaker problem. AI-generated explanations of physiological mechanisms are rarely overtly wrong. An interpretive framework proposed by means of this perspective states that explanations that appear plausible step by step may become become inconsistent when organ systems are considered together. It is therefore argued that the educator role is shifting from transmitting information to certifying coherence and proposes a classroom exercise, the error-hunt, for identifying seeded, systems-level inconsistencies in AI-generated explanations.

title: SparseTokenGS: Gaussian-based Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction via Reusable Token Pool
desc: Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography is widely used for fast, low-dose volumetric imaging and lesion localization in dentistry and image-guided interventions, but it introduces severe artifacts. Feed-forward Gaussian methods transfer the reconstruction cost to training and decode each coordinate from projection-aligned features and neighboring anchors. However, information from the whole scan is written only when the field is constructed and cannot be retrieved during coordinate decoding, leaving the volume inconsistent within the scan. This is a common limitation of such methods: once the field is fixed, decoding uses only local features and reconstruction quality drops substantially. We propose SparseTokenGS, a Gaussian-based method for sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography reconstruction via a reusable token pool. Anchor Token Fusion and Point-Token Attention query this shared pool at the anchors and at the query coordinates, respectively. The local Gaussian prior is retained, and the volume is reconstructed in one forward pass, without per-scan optimization or a projection-domain loss. On three public chest and dental datasets, SparseTokenGS achieves the highest reconstruction performance among the compared methods. On clinical dental scans, reconstruction from only six projections reaches 29.51 decibels in peak signal-to-noise ratio and a structural similarity of 0.842 against the full-view reference, and off-the-shelf tooth-and-pulp segmentation keeps these structures separable for root-canal localization. Experiments on volcanic rock and chicken show performance after same-object adaptation. A reusable token pool gives feed-forward reconstruction a mechanism that keeps scan-wide context available through decoding and can benefit future rapid clinical lesion localization and analysis. The code is available at: https://github.com/FrankDengAI/SparseTokenGS.

title: Deep-learning-based contrast synthesis in knee magnetic resonance imaging: performance across multiple target contrasts.
desc: [Magma (New York, N.Y.)] Quantitative MRI has been held back, because it increases scan time on top of clinical protocols. In this cross-sectional study, we explore how accurately unmeasured contrasts can be synthesized from magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) data. MRF, T1-weighted (T1w), gadolinium-enhanced T1w fat-saturated (Gd T1w fs), and double-echo steady-state (DESS) data were acquired at 3 T from volunteers having knee joint symptoms (n=88). Ten subjects were excluded due to missing MRF-data. U-Nets were trained to synthesize the other contrasts out of the MRF data, and the image quality was evaluated for both the synthetic and conventional by two radiologists. Presence of synovitis was evaluated from Gd T1w fs images. Wilcoxon signed-rank test was utilized to test differences in the image quality scores. Synthetic images overall had only slightly lower image quality in radiologists' evaluation for T1w (3.54 vs 3.88, p<0.01), DESS (3.22 vs 3.90, p<0.01), and Gd T1w fs images (3.40 vs 3.76, p<0.01). Synovitis could not be reliably observed from synthetic Gd T1w fs images. The image quality gap observed earlier persisted in this study and manifested itself steadily across all the joint tissues. Synovitis assessment was not possible from the synthetic contrast-enhanced images.

title: Silhouette-Based Gaitomics for Frailty Assessment in Older Adults
desc: Walking offers a window into physical function that may support interpretable video-based frailty assessment. We developed silhouette-based "gaitomics" to connect frailty predictions with measurable patterns of body configuration and movement. In 66 older adults assessed using the Fried Frailty Phenotype, standardized silhouettes and gait energy images yielded 90 descriptors of shape, temporal variation, motion, and texture. Minimum redundancy maximum relevance selection using the mutual information difference criterion prioritized informative features while limiting redundancy. Each classifier was evaluated using nested stratified cross-validation with five outer and three inner folds at the participant level, with feature ranking and feature-count selection confined to training partitions. Shapley additive explanations examined contributions to held-out predictions. Bilateral silhouette difference led the aggregate feature-selection rankings for three-class classification and both comparisons involving frail participants. Attribution profiles differed across tasks, with texture and consecutive-frame silhouette differences prominent in three-class classification. Among classifier-specific evaluations, CatBoost achieved the highest mean three-class micro-AUC of 0.647 \pm 0.085. Leading pairwise mean micro-AUCs were 0.833 \pm 0.249 for frail versus nonfrail, 0.765 \pm 0.168 for frail versus prefrail, and 0.554 \pm 0.129 for prefrail versus nonfrail classification. These findings connect model predictions to explicit gait characteristics while revealing task-dependent feature priorities and limited separation of prefrail and nonfrail participants. The framework provides an interpretable basis for further investigation, with larger independent studies needed to establish reliability and clinical relevance.

title: From Artificial to Embodied and Physical Intelligence in Smart Manufacturing.
desc: [Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany)] Manufacturing is evolving from automation-centered production toward systems capable of sensing, adaptation, and autonomous response across digital, mechanical, and material domains. Although recent progress has been largely driven by artificial intelligence, current manufacturing intelligence often remains external to physical systems and suffers from limited robustness, interpretability, and transferability in complex industrial environments. Here, we present a unified perspective on smart manufacturing through the framework of artificial intelligence (AI), embodied intelligence (EI), and physical intelligence (PI). AI provides abstraction, prediction, and generative capability; EI enables closed-loop perception, decision-making, and physical interaction; and PI embeds adaptive intelligence directly into materials, structures, and physicochemical processes. We further discuss how generative intelligence is beginning to connect these domains through inverse design, adaptive fabrication, and physics-constrained behavior realization. Recent advances in collaborative robotics, embodied digital twins, self-optimizing production systems, and physically intelligent materials, including self-actuating, self-healing, multistable, and shape-morphing systems, are reviewed. Finally, we propose an integrated AI-EI-PI framework spanning the full manufacturing lifecycle, highlighting a transition toward manufacturing systems in which intelligence is increasingly co-designed across algorithms, embodied agents, and matter itself.

title: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated Finite-Element Formulation in JAX for Large-Deformation Shells with Contact: Application to Patient-Specific Aortic Valve Simulation
desc: Patient-specific aortic-valve models can help assess how tissue properties and geometry influence leaflet deformation and coaptation, with potential to inform intervention planning. Large deformations, near-incompressibility, and evolving contact make these simulations computationally demanding and can challenge nonlinear convergence. Differentiable, GPU-accelerated methods offer efficient derivative evaluation and parallel computation, but their matrix-free application to soft-tissue shells with contact remains less established. We developed a forward solver using tatva's energy-based finite-element framework in JAX. The solver combines finite-strain extensible-director shells, hyperelastic constitutive models, and a finite-range repulsive contact energy. Nonlinear equilibrium is solved using a regularized, matrix-free Newton-Krylov method with two-level preconditioning. Automatic differentiation evaluates tangent-vector products without forming or storing the primary tangent matrix, while GPU execution parallelizes element and quadrature-point computations. Constitutive, shell, contact, and self-contact responses were assessed against analytical, semi-analytical, and published benchmarks. At a contact-free plate equilibrium, implicit sensitivities of the converged apex displacement to constitutive parameters, thickness, and pressure agreed with finite differences from independent nonlinear simulations. Simulations of three patient-specific aortic-valve models (two tricuspid and one bicuspid) achieved final relative equilibrium residuals below 10^-4. Median GPU runtimes were approximately 15-25 minutes, with 5.3-6.5-fold speedups relative to corresponding CPU runs on the tested hardware. These results provide component-level verification and demonstrate GPU-accelerated forward valve simulation in the tested cases, supporting future gradient-based inverse studies.

title: The Impact of Configurational Fit of Product and Service on Customer Decision-Making: Evidence from an Event-Related Potential Experiment.
desc: [Behavioral sciences (Basel, Switzerland)] Artificial intelligence provides new approaches for smart product-service systems. As such, an increasing number of service-oriented manufacturing enterprises are leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) to achieve value co-creation with customers. In the process of intelligently matching additional services to products, measuring the congruity of product-service systems remains to be explored. This study employs an event-related potential (ERP) methodology to examine how product-service congruity influences customer purchase intentions associated with cognitive processing. ERPs elicited by high-congruity product-service combinations were significantly different from low-congruity combinations. By proposing a method to determine product-service congruity, this study provides insights for matching product-service combinations in an AI-driven context. These findings can guide the delivery of enhanced personalized product-service combinations in platform economies and AI ecosystems, enabling enterprises to achieve value co-creation.

title: Meta-Initialization of Implicit Neural Representations to Accelerate Deformable Medical Image Registration
desc: Implicit neural representation (INR) methods for deformable medical image registration require the network parameters to be optimized for each new image pair, making adaptation speed a practical limitation. This work investigates whether early adaptation can be accelerated using an initialization learned from a collection of previously solved registration tasks. We examine two schemes: Reptile meta-initialization and STRAINER transfer of the shared component of a coordinate network. KAN-IDIR is used as the base INR displacement-field model. Experiments are conducted on OASIS-1, with 364 consecutive pairs used for training and 49 pairs for test-time adaptation. Registration quality is evaluated using mean Dice and HD95, together with the fraction of voxels with a negative Jacobian determinant at iteration 1500. In the configurations studied, both schemes yield higher Dice and lower HD95 at early iterations than random initialization. Reptile numerically outperforms STRAINER under a small iteration budget, although their pretraining budgets are not matched. As the number of iterations increases, the differences between the schemes shrink. STRAINER pretraining takes 39-40 minutes, compared with 44.98 hours for Reptile.

title: A user-friendly platform for deep-learning-based image enhancement in scanning X-ray microscopy.
desc: [Journal of synchrotron radiation] Images acquired by scanning X-ray microscopy are often limited in spatial resolution by the finite size and profile of the scanning probe. Here, we present a dedicated graphical user interface for physics-informed image enhancement that incorporates the experimentally characterized probe to decouple probe-induced blurring from the measured images. The software integrates experimentally reconstructed probe intensity into the model training and provides an end-to-end workflow for image super-resolution and deblurring. We demonstrate the approach using differential phase-contrast imaging, where the finite scanning probe limits the recovery of fine spatial features. The enhanced images recover spatial details beyond those directly resolved in the measured data. This platform provides a practical and reproducible tool for physics-informed image enhancement during synchrotron X-ray microscopy experiments.

title: Particle-adapted next-generation risk assessment of micro- and nanoplastics from food contact materials: Integrating PBK/PBTK, AOPs and explainable artificial intelligence.
source: PubMed · Toxicology in vitro : an international journal published in association with BIBRA
desc: [Toxicology in vitro : an international journal published in association with BIBRA] Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) released from food contact materials (FCMs) present a risk-assessment challenge because exposure depends not only on mass concentration but also on particle size, number, morphology, polymer identity, surface properties, aggregation, transformation, and co-migration of additives and non-intentionally added substances. Conventional approaches remain fragmented and are poorly suited to translating FCM-specific particle release into human-relevant internal dosimetry and mechanistic toxicity. This review proposes a particle-adapted next-generation risk assessment (NGRA) framework integrating FCM release characterization, gastrointestinal transformation and absorbed fraction, physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBK/PBTK) modelling, adverse outcome pathways (AOPs), and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). The framework explicitly defines data hand-offs between modules, including particle-specific exposure metrics, internal particle burden, persistence and clearance parameters, key-event evidence, and model uncertainty. AOPs are used to organize mechanistic evidence rather than infer causality, while XAI is positioned as an interpretability and prioritization tool subject to applicability-domain assessment, external validation, reproducibility, and uncertainty analysis. Attention is given to distinguishing particle-mediated effects from those associated with co-migrating additives and non-intentionally added substances. Regulatory translation is considered in the context of FCM migration assessment and emerging NAM-based approaches. The framework provides a basis for evidence integration, testing prioritization, and future quantitative regulatory assessment of FCM-derived MNPs.

title: Emerging Technologies for the Discovery and Characterization of Microbial Natural Products.
desc: [Chimia] The discovery of natural products has changed dramatically in recent years, and new technologies have been developed continuously to improve this process, including the integration of artificial intelligence tools. Herein, we summarize some emerging methodologies, including genome mining, activation of selected biosynthetic pathways, chemical probes, and mass spectrometry-based metabolomics. Selected examples are discussed in detail, highlighting and describing their discovery strategies.

title: A Cross-Scale 3D Attention and Boundary-Aware Network for Sea-Land Segmentation.
desc: [Journal of imaging] Coastal segmentation struggles with complex terrain configurations and discontinuous edge demarcation. To resolve these challenges, we propose a novel deep learning model, the Cross-Scale Attention and Boundary-Aware Network (CABANet). The network synergistically enhances segmentation performance through two core innovations. First, we design a Cross-Scale 3D Attention Fusion Module, which creatively stacks multi-scale 2D feature maps from the backbone into a pseudo-3D feature volume. It then performs efficient contextual modeling across different geographic scales via a decomposed 3D attention mechanism, generating a highly optimized semantic summary feature. Second, we design a boundary enhancement module to strengthen the extraction and analysis of boundary features and improve the segmentation of the sea-land boundary, while utilizing contextual information to guide the boundary enhancement process. Evaluations on Landsat-8 OLI and SLSD datasets confirm state-of-the-art performance in both regional homogeneity and edge continuity.

title: Natural, Artificial, and Human Intelligences.
desc: [Journal of Intelligence] Human achievement, whether in culture, science, or technology, is unparalleled in the known existence. This achievement is tied to the enormous communities of knowledge, made possible by language. We trace how the principle '᾿Eν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος' (in the beginning was the word) was extended beyond its theological origins and heightened the value of written intelligence throughout Western societies. There lies the challenge regarding modern-age chatbots: they can 'do' language apparently as well as ourselves, and there is a natural question of whether they can be considered intelligent, in the same way as we are or otherwise. Are humans uniquely intelligent? We consider this question in terms of the psychological literature on intelligence, evidence for intelligence in non-human animals, the role of written language in science and technology, progress with artificial intelligence, the history of intelligence testing (for both humans and machines), and the role of embodiment in intelligence. We think that it is increasingly difficult to consider humans uniquely intelligent. There are current limitations in chatbots, e.g., concerning perceptual and social awareness, but much attention is currently devoted to overcoming such limitations.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Identification and Experimental Validation of COX-2 and ERK1/2 as Anti-Inflammatory Targets of Avenanthramides.
desc: [Nutrients] Chronic low-grade inflammation underlies numerous chronic diseases, yet the molecular targets of dietary bioactive compounds remain largely unknown. We developed a deep learning model integrating heterogeneous network propagation, stacked denoising autoencoders, and a CNN classifier to predict inflammation-related targets of food-derived compounds. The model was validated by cross-validation and on eight compounds from distinct structural categories. Avn A, Avn B, and Avn C were then input into the model to predict their anti-inflammatory targets, followed by network analysis, docking, and cellular assays for validation. The model achieved a mean AUC of 0.9587 and an AUPR of 0.9590, with validation on eight structurally diverse compounds confirming its generalizability. For Avn A, Avn B, and Avn C, 118 overlapping anti-inflammatory targets were predicted. Network analysis and KEGG pathway enrichment identified ERK1/2 as a key node within the MAPK and PI3K-AKT signaling pathways, while COX-2 was prioritized for further validation based on its high prediction score. Molecular docking revealed that Avns bound at the cyclooxygenase channel entrance of COX-2 with binding energies of -7.7 to -8.0 kcal/mol, and at the ATP-binding pockets of ERK1/2 with binding energies of -7.0 to -7.7 kcal/mol. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, Avns dose-dependently inhibited COX-2 enzymatic activity and PGE2 production, attenuated ERK1/2 and c-Fos phosphorylation, and suppressed IL-6 and IL-1β expression. Our deep learning model successfully identified COX-2 and ERK1/2 as key mediators of the anti-inflammatory effects of Avns, revealing a dual mechanism involving COX-2 inhibition and ERK/c-Fos pathway blockade. This study provides new evidence for the molecular targets of Avns and demonstrates the utility of deep learning-based approaches for target discovery of dietary bioactive compounds.
